paragraphs.text: Collapsible plugin/global-panel section for the DeepSeek Harness sidebar
# dsh-sidebar-fold

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that
makes the left sidebar's **plugin / global-panel entry section collap

sible**.
When many plugins register a `sidebar.panellist` entry, that list grows and
squeezes the wo

rkspace/session browser below it. This plugin adds a compact
section header above the list: one clic

k folds every entry away and returns the
vertical space to the workspace region; another click resto

very entry away and returns the
vertical space to the workspace region; another click restores them.

- Works with the shipped 0.2.x sidebar (drawer, pins, "more" menu, shortcuts
all keep working) — it

observes the `nav[aria-label]` landmark instead of
importing or replacing any plugin component.
- On

ly in the **expanded** column and only with **2+ entries**; the 56px rail
keeps its icon column, and

a single entry adds no chrome.
- The fold header shows a count badge while folded, carries
`aria-ex

panded` / `aria-controls`, and localizes its label (中文 `面板` /
English `Panels`).
- Fold state is tra

nsient view state that resets on reload, matching the
shell's own collapse handling.
- No host-side
behavior, no tools, no storage, no network. Client-only.

## What it registers
The `cordis.patch.yml` layer inserts one row:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The package declares `dsh.client.platform: web` and `exports["./client"]`, so
the browser module tab

le picks up `lib/client.js`. The host entry
(`lib/index.js`) is an empty `apply()` — required so the

Loader mounts the row,
but with no host-side effects.
## Verify locally
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`npm test` covers: no fold row for a single entry, no fold row in the rail,
fold/restores all rows w
ith a count badge, and full cleanup on dispose.
## How it works

`apply(ctx)` installs a `MutationObserver` on `document.body`. On each sidebar
render it finds the p

anel list, inserts (or refreshes) the fold header before
it, and reflects the folded state with inli

ne styles. The callback
disconnects before writing and reconnects afterwards, so its own DOM writes

never re-trigger it; every write is idempotent. `ctx.effect()` releases the
observer, the injected r

ow, and all inline styles when the client fiber is
disposed (HMR safe).
